procedure.method: Independently inspected the displayed raster returned by tools.view_image(detail='original'), forwarded through functions.exec's image helper. First viewed pinned A1 original.png, then R7-B05-M1 native, usage720 and thumbnail320, in that packet order and in separate calls. All three poster views were displayed before any transcription judgment, fidelity judgment or score. Read the pinned source and poster manifests before comparison; the packet supplies no protected-layout manifest. Verified all 13 explicitly permitted input files against their pinned SHA-256 and byte sizes, and checked PNG-header dimensions. After viewing, compared source placement with the native poster using a read-only standard-library PNG decode and a declared blue-pixel threshold. No image was generated, edited, cropped or written; no embedded unpinned path was followed. No session/thread ID was inferred.

content_form.observation: The complete cobalt blue ribbon artwork, with its large upper-left loop and smaller lower-right loop, is the dominant nonglyph subject. Its recognisable form directly supplies the artist/open-studio content.

content_form.location: Middle of poster, above the four footer lines
content_form.observation: Both loop interiors, the crossing band, mounting pegs and wall shadows remain visible at use size. The artwork has substantial scale rather than functioning as a small decorative accent.

hierarchy.location: Upper-left title, central blue artwork and lower-left footer
hierarchy.observation: The bold title remains identifiable and the blue double-loop silhouette remains the strongest nonglyph focus. The smaller artist line and bottom information block form clear supporting levels.
Date/time and address are larger than the descriptive and reservation lines and sit below the complete artwork, so practical visit information is easy to find without covering it.

typography.location: Title and artist line at upper left

typography.observation: All six required copy entries are readable across the poster. The footer retains the date periods, time colons and range dash, address comma, and contiguous URL punctuation.

The descriptive and reservation copy becomes very small at 256×320; the complete URL cannot be confidently read at this scale alone. It remains legible in the previously viewed native and usage720 views.

space.location: Left edges of header and footer, approximately x96–100
space.observation: Title, artist line and all footer lines share a nearly common left margin. The top margin, short header-to-art gap, art-to-date gap and bottom margin form deliberate separation rather than crowded overlays.

space.location: Wall within the two loops and around the right-hand contour
space.observation: The open wall areas preserve the sculpture's negative spaces and cast shadows. The complete right loop stays inside the frame, and the footer sits in the wall area beneath it.

image_material.location: Blue band surfaces, two brass mounting points and rightward wall shadows
image_material.observation: The cobalt ribbon retains the source-specific large/small loop geometry, twisting band, painterly surface and plausible wall contact. Light, surface texture and shadows read as a coherent photograph-style image.

image_material.location: Artwork's upper and lower extents, compared with source A1
image_material.observation: The artwork retains approximately the same size, proportions and blue colour family, but its position is displaced downward: the source blue-pixel bounds begin at y239 and the poster's at y268. This is a preservation-condition failure despite strong local material construction.

emotion_control.location: Warm off-white wall, blue sculpture and soft cast shadows
emotion_control.observation: The photographed wall texture and gentle light convey a quiet, intimate viewing atmosphere grounded in the actual supplied artwork. The specific blue object carries the mood without added faces or invented studio props.

emotion_control.location: Black header and footer surrounding the photograph
emotion_control.observation: The firm title supplies an event announcement while the smaller supporting text lets the artwork and light remain prominent. The restrained text treatment is coherent with this observed open-studio photograph.

ai_slop.location: Whole poster, especially artwork crossings and footer copy
ai_slop.observation: There are no observable extra tools, faces, logos, sponsors, invented labels or arbitrary decorative motifs. The two loops and crossing band remain structurally coherent and the required text is intact.

The layout uses the substantial supplied visual and useful information without token ornaments or contradictory scene additions. The small source-placement drift is documented explicitly rather than being treated as perfect preservation.

residuals: Source-placement fidelity: the artwork is shifted downward by about 29 pixels (about 2.1% of native frame height); source and poster blue-mask bounds are recorded separately.
At thumbnail320 the smallest descriptive and reservation lines are too small for reliable full transcription; they were read from the native view after all three views were inspected.

The left/front blue band appears slightly brighter and its local brush marks are not pixel-identical to A1. The recognisable identity, colour family and proportions remain; no redraw or substitution is inferred from pixel differences alone.

source_comparison_measurements.method: Read-only PNG decoding; inclusive bounds of pixels satisfying B>75, B>1.35R, B>1.15G and B-R>40. These are blue-surface bounds, not a protected-layout manifest or exact outer-shadow segmentation.
source_comparison_measurements.interpretation: The visually compared mounting points also move approximately 30 pixels downward. Scale/proportions and colour family are retained, but the specified wall-hung position is changed.
